rewrite.summary: This project focuses on the frame and suspension modifications of a Suburban, including removing old cross members and installing new ones with improved reinforcement. The build aims to provide enhanced articulation capabilities.
rewrite.rewritten_article_markdown:
This project focuses on the frame and suspension modifications of a Suburban, including removing old cross members and installing new ones with improved reinforcement. The build aims to provide enhanced articulation capabilities.

The back of the truck had three cross members that were all in the way. With a panhard mount, shock mounts, winch mount, relocated gas tank mounts, and general frame strengthening support needed, it all had to come out and be redesigned.

Old x-members:
![](http://i14.photobucket.com/albums/a307/bonedust213/truck/post-1-0-45016800-1295303656_thumb.jpg)

And removed:
![](http://i14.photobucket.com/albums/a307/bonedust213/truck/post-1-0-09137000-1295303761_thumb.jpg)

The frame was plated in where the new x-member will live. The front and back of the frame were tied together using L-shaped gussets.
![](http://i14.photobucket.com/albums/a307/bonedust213/truck/post-1-0-15558600-1295303790_thumb.jpg)

A new x-member, including a panhard mount, was fabricated and installed.
![](http://i14.photobucket.com/albums/a307/bonedust213/truck/post-1-0-80473800-1295303862_thumb.jpg)

The x-member was test fitted to show how the pass-throughs for body mounts work.
![](http://i14.photobucket.com/albums/a307/bonedust213/truck/post-1-0-82933000-1295304906_thumb.jpg)

The x-member was fully welded in and the rear suspension components were installed, including one rear link and a radius arm.
![](http://i14.photobucket.com/albums/a307/bonedust213/truck/post-1-0-45534600-1295305376_thumb.jpg)

post_rewrites.rewritten_content:
Part one can be found here: [http://www.fullsizechevy.com/forum/g...assult-v2.html](http://www.fullsizechevy.com/forum/g...assult-v2.html)

Why part 2? Part 1 generated some concerns about the timeline of this project, but I assure you that I have full control. To avoid any further public debates, we will focus solely on discussing the truck itself. Here are a few points to address potential questions:

1. No solid finish date other than "as soon as possible."
2. Cost details are not relevant; home-built SAS projects can exceed this cost.
3. The rear cross members were removed and redesigned for a panhard mount, shock mounts, winch attachment, gas tank relocation, and general frame reinforcement.

The old x-members supported two of the rear body mounts, which will be addressed in more detail later. The new x-member will be plated where it is needed, and L-shaped gussets were used to connect the front and back of the frame.
This component requires a new installation. It involves replacing the OEM x-member support with a replica, along with a fresh x-member/panhard mount cut from a plasma table.
I'm glad to see it coming together.

Originally posted by bonedust:  
Beautiful work as always. The 10-inch pictures are stunning.

Here is the X-member being test-fitted, showing how the body mounts pass through and are secured in place. Clearancing marks indicate where additional space is needed for the top corner of the tire during full articulation. Cut lines have been marked and made using a cordless Makita saw. Clay notes that it easily passes through a 1/4 plate obstacle with minimal issues. I need to get one of those.
This image illustrates the scale of the build. On the right is a 3/4 Heim joint, the middle features an FK joint commonly found in monster trucks, and on the left is a rear link radius arm.
